# Evaluating ocean forecasting systems

OceanBench is a benchmarking tool to evaluate ocean forecasting systems against reference ocean analysis datasets (such as 2024 [GLORYS reanalysis](https://data.marine.copernicus.eu/product/GLOBAL_MULTIYEAR_PHY_001_030) and [GLO12 analysis](https://data.marine.copernicus.eu/product/GLOBAL_ANALYSISFORECAST_PHY_001_024)) as well as in-situ and satellite observations.

Evaluating ocean forecast performance is a complex task, as different users have varying priorities.
Some may focus on accurate predictions of currents, while others prioritize sea level or salinity forecasts.
To accommodate these diverse needs, OceanBench provides a comprehensive set of metrics.
Please keep in mind that these metrics capture key aspects of forecast quality rather than the complete picture.

Want to evaluate your system or get involved in OceanBench? Check out the [GitHub project](https://github.com/mercator-ocean/oceanbench/)!

Most challenger forecasts are produced by running each system at [Mercator Ocean International](https://www.mercator-ocean.eu/); the [Challengers](challengers/index.qmd) page shows who ran each forecast.

For the 1 degree track, the interpolation method used for challengers, the corresponding reference datasets, and the exact implementation paths are documented [here](documentation/one-degree-track/index.qmd).

## Comparison to observations <span class="source-icons"><span class="source-icon argo-profiler" role="img" aria-label="Argo profiler" title="Argo profiler"></span><span class="source-icon drifter-buoy" role="img" aria-label="Surface drifter" title="Surface drifter"></span><span class="source-icon satellite" role="img" aria-label="Satellite altimetry" title="Satellite altimetry"></span></span> {#comparison-to-observations}

Absolute RMSD scores against 2024 [Argo profiles and surface drifters](https://data.marine.copernicus.eu/product/INSITU_GLO_PHY_UV_DISCRETE_NRT_013_048) (temperature, salinity, velocity) and [along-track altimetry](https://data.marine.copernicus.eu/product/SEALEVEL_GLO_PHY_L3_MY_008_062) (sea level anomaly) observations (Class IV validation). The colors denote % difference to the selected baseline. See the [evaluation method](evaluation-methods/index.qmd#evaluation-methods-observations).

<div id="observations-scores"></div>

## Smoothing-controlled RMSD <span class="source-icons"><span class="source-icon argo-profiler" role="img" aria-label="Argo profiler" title="Argo profiler"></span><span class="source-icon drifter-buoy" role="img" aria-label="Surface drifter" title="Surface drifter"></span><span class="source-icon satellite" role="img" aria-label="Satellite altimetry" title="Satellite altimetry"></span></span> {#smoothing-controlled-rmsd}

The RMSD against the same Class IV observations after the best Gaussian smoothing (0 to 90 km) and the best rescaling of the forecast departure from the GLORYS12 monthly climatology, fitted on every other forecast initialization day and scored on the others. Smoothing or damping a forecast cannot lower it, unlike the RMSD above, which stays the score of the forecast as issued. The fitted width and slope are shown below as diagnostics: a large width means the challenger is skillful only at large scales, a slope below 1 means its anomalies are too strong, above 1 too weak. Compare two challengers in a row only when they differ by at least 1.5 percent (2 percent for salinity, 2.5 percent for salinity at 0-5 m and 100-300 m) with a 90 percent bootstrap interval over initialization days that excludes zero; this floor is per comparison, and with this many rows a few differences will pass it by chance. See the [evaluation method](evaluation-methods/index.qmd#smoothing-controlled-rmsd-of-variables-compared-to-observations).

## Comparison to reanalysis <span class="source-icons"><span class="source-icon model-grid-globe" role="img" aria-label="Model" title="Model"></span></span> {#comparison-to-reanalysis}

Absolute RMSD scores against 2024 [GLORYS reanalysis](https://data.marine.copernicus.eu/product/GLOBAL_MULTIYEAR_PHY_001_030). These are the deterministic scores for the forecasted variables and physically consistent diagnostic variables. The colors denote % difference to the selected baseline. See the [evaluation method](evaluation-methods/index.qmd#evaluation-methods-reanalysis).
